analysis.investment_thesis: FSL is a mid-cap BPO stalwart with a compelling FY25 revenue acceleration (26% YoY to ₹7,980 Cr), but underlying earnings growth (~15%) yields a PEG of ~1.6x at the trailing P/E — stretching Lynch's GARP discipline. Surging debt (borrowings nearly doubled to ₹2,369 Cr in FY25) and declining free cash flow (₹744 Cr → ₹477 Cr over 3 years) undercut what is otherwise a decent multi-geography IT services story.
key_strengths: FY25 revenue surged 26% to ₹7,980 Cr — real top-line acceleration, likely acquisition-fueled, expanding into GenAI service lines
Strong promoter conviction at 53.66% + DII support at 25.49%; diversified across US/UK/India/UAE reduces single-market risk
Operating profit growing faster than revenue (EBIT CAGR 13.4% vs revenue CAGR 10.6%), showing margin discipline despite BPO's thin-margin nature
key_risks: PEG ~1.6x on trailing earnings growth (~15%) — Lynch's comfort zone is sub-1.0; not a bargain at 24x PE
Borrowings nearly doubled YoY (₹1,526 → ₹2,369 Cr); finance costs rose 19% to ₹184 Cr, eating into thin margins
Free cash flow deteriorating (₹744 Cr in FY23 → ₹477 Cr in FY25) despite revenue growth — capital allocation quality is declining
red_flags: Cash balance near zero: collapsed from ₹69 Cr to ₹13 Cr in one year — balance sheet fragility post-acquisition
Investing CF of -₹744 Cr in FY25 with near-zero disclosure on what was acquired — story opacity Lynch despises
Net profit CAGR of only 9.6% over 9 years for a 'tech-enabled' services firm is a slow-grower's track record, not a fast grower's
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Firstsource is a classic Lynch stalwart — a steadily growing BPO business serving healthcare, BFSI, and CMT verticals across three continents. The 9-year story is honest: 10.6% revenue CAGR, 9.6% earnings CAGR — dependable but not exciting. What changes the narrative is FY25's 26% revenue jump, which almost certainly reflects an inorganic move (investing outflow of ₹744 Cr, borrowings up ₹843 Cr in one year, cash drained to ₹13 Cr). Lynch would want to understand this acquisition before getting excited — "What did you buy, and at what price?"

The valuation math is the problem. At ₹239, trailing P/E of 24.1x against realistic earnings growth of 12–15% gives a PEG of 1.6–2.0x — Lynch's "overvalued for the growth rate" zone. The forward P/E of 18.1x implies the market is pricing in ~33% earnings growth, which requires the FY25 acquisition to integrate flawlessly and organic momentum to sustain. With FCF declining even as revenues grow, ROE stuck at 15%, and operating margins only 11.9%, this is not a company printing money efficiently. Worth watching for a cleaner entry post-acquisition integration, but not a buy today.
